memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: new patient establishing care for depression, iron-deficiency anaemia and asthma.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Ms reports low mood, fatigue, occasional wheeze and exertional dyspnoea for 3 months.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 27.2 (obese). Advised on reduced calorie intake and daily walk. Pallor noted, lungs clear with occasional wheeze.
IMPRESSION: 1) Depression, moderate severity. 2) Iron-deficiency anaemia, likely due to dietary insufficiency. 3) Persistent asthma, uncontrolled. Ordered fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar as per annual screening.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start sertraline 50 mg OD, ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Influenza vaccine not due (outside autumn). Return if: worsening sadness, suicidal thoughts, chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or bleeding per rectum.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Patient reports allergy to penicillin; develops widespread rash and pruritus within minutes of last dose taken 2 years ago.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Haemoglobin 9.8 g/dL (12-16), Serum ferritin 12 ng/mL (15-150), MCV 78 fL (80-100).
TSH 4.2 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), Vitamin B12 210 pg/mL (200-900).
PHQ-9 score 14 (0-27).
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 210 mg/dL (<200), LDL 130 mg/dL (<100), HDL 48 mg/dL (>40), Triglycerides 160 mg/dL (<150).
Fasting blood sugar 92 mg/dL (70-99).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of initial labs and symptom response.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says mood improved slightly, energy better, still occasional wheeze on exertion.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 67.5 kg, BMI 27.0 (obese). Diet and activity advice reiterated. Lungs: mild wheeze bilaterally.
IMPRESSION: Depression partially responsive; anaemia improving but still iron-deficient; asthma partially controlled. Continue current meds, consider increasing sertraline if needed.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase sertraline to 100 mg OD, keep ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, continue asthma meds. Influenza vaccine not due. Return if: worsening depression, suicidal ideation, chest pain, severe breathlessness, fever >39°C, or melena.

memories.text:
sertraline 100 mg OD
ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD
salbutamol metered-dose inhaler SOS

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Spirometry with reversibility: Pre-bronchodilator FEV1 2.1 L (80% predicted), FVC 2.8 L (85% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.75. Post-salbutamol FEV1 2.4 L (12% increase), FVC 2.9 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83. Indicates reversible airway obstruction consistent with asthma.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: asthma review after spirometry.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports reduced wheeze, able to walk 2 km without symptoms, occasional night cough.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 67 kg, BMI 26.9 (overweight). Advised on weight reduction. Lungs: occasional wheeze at lung bases.
IMPRESSION: Asthma control improved but not optimal; depression stable on sertraline 100 mg; anaemia unchanged. Consider stepping up inhaled steroid.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase budesonide-formoterol to 400/12 inhaler BD, continue other meds. Influenza vaccine not due. Return if: worsening cough, night awakenings, chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or haematemesis.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: Feeling better overall, mood good, still using salbutamol 2-3 times/week for wheeze. No side effects from meds. Will attend follow-up as scheduled.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of labs and ongoing symptoms.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports persistent low mood, fatigue, and occasional wheeze during night shifts.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/82 mmHg, weight 66.5 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Advised on continued calorie control and activity. Lungs: mild wheeze.
IMPRESSION: Depression partially responsive; consider switching to escitalopram for better tolerability. Anaemia improving but still borderline; asthma mild intermittent.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop sertraline, start escitalopram 10 mg OD. Continue ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, asthma meds as is. Influenza vaccine offered and given today (0.5 mL IM). Return if: worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, chest pain, severe breathlessness, fever >39°C, or rectal bleeding.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Dr Suresh Kumar, Psychiatrist, for management of treatment-resistant depression. Patient has tried sertraline and escitalopram with partial response; requests adjunctive therapy and counselling.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Psychiatrist response: Patient assessed, diagnosis moderate depressive disorder. Recommend continuing escitalopram 10 mg OD, adding cognitive behavioural therapy, and reviewing in 6 weeks. No medication change advised at present.
